Today’s failing approach: reskilling programs assign AI training without assessing AI skills
task_alt
Course completion records
A completion record shows that an employee finished an AI course. The record does not show whether the employee can use AI to complete a work task.
thumbs_up_down
Self-assessment surveys
Employees rate their own confidence with AI tools. Two employees can give the same rating for different levels of skill.
how_to_reg
Manager nominations
Managers choose who joins which training track. Different managers can use different criteria for the same choice.
One course for every team
A single AI course for the whole company can spend training time on skills that some employees already have.
Your program team then assigns training without a comparable measure of each employee’s current AI skills.

Place engineers in AI training tracks by assessed proficiency level
For engineering teams, your reskilling program uses the Tech section of Skills Intelligence.
Engineers complete coding tasks in a realistic development environment.
You enable or disable the AI Assistant for each assessment.
Codility captures every interaction with the AI Assistant as reviewable AI activity. The AI activity does not affect automated scoring.
Codility’s Engineering Skills Model groups AI skills into categories, including AI Evaluation, AI Application and AI Building.
Passed test cases and task difficulty set a proficiency level for each assessed skill. The scale runs from novice to expert across five levels.
Your program team can place each engineer in a training track based on the proficiency levels measured in the assessment.

Frequently asked questions about AI skills assessment for reskilling programs
An AI skills assessment for reskilling programs tests how employees complete work tasks with AI before training starts. Codility Skills Intelligence runs this assessment for employees in business roles and engineering. Your program team uses each result to decide who takes which training.
Yes, if the company decides who takes which training. A training record shows that an employee completed a course. An AI skills assessment shows how the employee performed on a task with AI.
Assess the employees on a realistic task with AI before the program starts. Codility scores each output. Your program team then compares the results by employee and by team and assigns the training.
Add an AI skills assessment. Keep the training platform for the courses. Skills Intelligence gives each employee a realistic task to complete with AI and scores the output. Your program team can then see which results show a training gap.
No. An AI skills assessment and a reskilling platform do different jobs. Skills Intelligence assesses skills, and your reskilling platform delivers the courses.
The assessment covers business roles and engineering roles. For business roles without role-specific tasks, Skills Intelligence offers general workforce tasks.
Yes. Each employee sees assessed results in a personal profile.
Your program team makes the training decisions. Codility provides the assessed results.
Introduce the assessment as the step that places employees into training based on their current skills. Explain how your program team will use the results before the assessment starts.
Yes, through Codility Screen. See the AI capability assessment page for supported roles and current access.
Plan an AI skills assessment pilot for your reskilling program
Tell us which job family you want to assess before training starts. A Codility specialist will contact you about a scoped pilot for that job family.
